title: The Footprint Library — Anonymized Alumni Journeys as Browsable Artifacts
concept:
=== APPROVED PRODUCT BRIEF (the user picked this from a 5-brief set; build EXACTLY this) ===

Frame: radical-reinterpretation (probability 0.05)
Title: The Footprint Library — Anonymized Alumni Journeys as Browsable Artifacts
Thesis: Turn opted-in alumni CLR histories into anonymized, semantically searchable case-study footprints a first-year can study quietly, with optional one-message escalation.
Why this frame: Reframes the alumni network as a corpus, not a roster — async-forever, not synchronous-now. Resolves FERPA, opt-in fatigue, and Teams-introduction burden in one move by making the live alumnus optional rather than central.

PRIMARY PERSONA:
  Name: Jamal Williams
  Role: First-year, first-generation undergraduate, intended Computer Science major
  Context: Six weeks into his first semester at Northeastern. Failing Fundamentals of CS 1, lurks on r/Northeastern and r/csMajors late at night, hasn't booked a single advisor meeting because the idea of admitting he's struggling out loud feels worse than struggling.
  Emotional state: Quietly panicked. Performs fine to family. Suspects he doesn't belong. Comforted by long anonymous narratives where someone else describes the same feeling.
  Pain points:
    - Live introductions to alumni feel like a job interview he hasn't prepared for
    - 'Success stories' on the university website feature seniors at FAANG who he can't relate to at week 6
    - NU Source feels abandoned and the UI signals nobody is actually there
    - He doesn't know what he doesn't know — generic advice ('go to office hours!') skips the specific shame loop he's in
  JTBD: When I'm quietly drowning in week 6 of freshman year, I want to read about someone who was here too and made it out, so I can keep going without having to perform composure for a stranger.
SECONDARY ACTORS:
  - Opted-in Alumni Contributor (Trailblazer): Reviews and approves an AI-drafted anonymized version of their own first-year journey, sets escalation availability (e.g. 'open to one message per month').
  - Liz (Co-op Strategy Lead, NXT Humans engagement sponsor): Owns library coverage curation, approves anonymization templates, monitors coverage-gap dashboard, signs off on tone/appropriateness.
  - IT M365 Admin: Operates the SharePoint corpus, Azure OpenAI indexing job, Power Automate escalation flows, FERPA audit logging.
  - Co-op Faculty Advisor: Can prescribe Library searches as homework, sees aggregated (never individual) themes students are searching for.

DEMONSTRATED MOMENT: Jamal types a raw sentence about failing his first CS class into the Footprint Library inside Teams. Within two seconds, three anonymized alumni journeys surface — each one a 4-minute readable arc, each with the same week-6 inflection point he's living right now. He reads one. At the end, a single quiet line: 'This alum is open to one message if you'd like.' He's not matched. He's invited.

USE CASES (11) — the prototype MUST demonstrate at least 5 of these as live flows:
  1. Natural-Language Footprint Search
     Trigger: Jamal opens the Footprint Library tab inside Microsoft Teams at 1:47 AM and types 'I'm failing my first CS class and feel like I don't belong here' into a single search field.
     Flow: (1) Query is embedded via Azure OpenAI. (2) Semantic vector search runs against the anonymized SharePoint corpus, scoring by skill-gap similarity, emotional-arc similarity, and demographic-context similarity (with FERPA guardrails). (3) Top 3 footprints surface with a Match Confidence band (Resonant / Adjacent / Distant) and a one-sentence 'why this one' from the model. (4) Jamal taps the most resonant card.
     AI role: Embeds the messy natural-language query, performs hybrid semantic + structured CLR-skill search, generates the one-sentence rationale for each match.
     Outcome: Jamal sees three case studies that feel uncannily aligned with his actual moment — not three LinkedIn profiles, not three job postings.
  2. Anonymized Journey Reader
     Trigger: Jamal selects the top-matched footprint titled 'A Footprint from a CS first-year, Fall 2019'.
     Flow: (1) A long-form, editorially formatted narrative loads — no avatar, no name, no employer logos. (2) Chapter markers: 'Week 1', 'Week 6 (the wall)', 'Spring recovery', 'First co-op'. (3) Inline CLR competency tags appear in the margin showing what skills were forming and at what pace. (4) Read time estimate (~4 minutes) anchored top-right. (5) Reading progress is privately tracked for Jamal's reflection journal.
     AI role: Renders the synthesized narrative from raw CLR evidence; surfaces margin annotations linking prose to skill data.
     Outcome: Jamal reads something that feels like a New Yorker short story about himself, written from the other side of the wall.
  3. Inflection-Point Highlighting
     Trigger: As Jamal scrolls, he reaches the 'Week 6' chapter.
     Flow: (1) A soft margin highlight animates in. (2) A pill labeled 'Inflection point — this is where the trajectory turned' appears. (3) Below the prose, a small CLR mini-chart shows the alum's Python proficiency score over the next 8 weeks — flat, then climbing. (4) Jamal taps the pill to see what specific actions the alum took.
     AI role: Detects longitudinal inflection points in the alum's CLR record using time-series analysis on competency scores; pairs the data signal with the prose moment.
     Outcome: Jamal sees that the wall is a real, named, common thing — and that climbing it is also a real, named, common thing.
  4. Save to My CLR Reflection
     Trigger: At the end of the journey, Jamal taps 'Save to my reflection'.
     Flow: (1) The footprint is bookmarked into Jamal's private CLR Reflection space in SharePoint. (2) Copilot drafts a 2-sentence reflection prompt tailored to this footprint ('What part of this week-6 chapter felt closest to your own week?'). (3) Jamal can answer or skip. (4) Reflections feed back (privately) into Jamal's own emerging CLR profile as evidence of metacognition.
     AI role: Generates personalized reflection prompts grounded in both the saved footprint and Jamal's current CLR signals.
     Outcome: Reading becomes an active CLR-building activity, not passive consumption. Liz can later cite 'metacognitive reflection volume' as a real metric.
  5. Optional 'Unmask & Connect' Escalation
     Trigger: At the very bottom of the reader, after Jamal has scrolled through the full arc, a single quiet line appears: 'This alum is open to one message if you'd like.'
     Flow: (1) Jamal taps. (2) A consent screen appears: what will be shared (his first name, his message, NO CLR skill data), what won't, alum's response-time expectation. (3) Jamal writes a short message. Copilot offers a structured prompt scaffold ('I just read your footprint. The part about week 6 hit me because...'). (4) Power Automate posts a Teams DM to the alum with Jamal's note + the footprint context. (5) The alum can reply, decline, or set boundaries. No CLR data crosses the boundary without double opt-in.
     AI role: Provides conversation scaffolding, runs the FERPA pre-flight check on what data is leaving Jamal's profile, drafts the Teams intro message.
     Outcome: If Jamal wants the conversation, he gets one — on his terms, after he's read enough to feel ready. If he doesn't, the value was already delivered.
  6. Alumni Footprint Contribution Flow
     Trigger: An opted-in alum, Sarah (class of '20), receives a Power Automate invite in Teams: 'Your first-year journey could help someone this week. 15 minutes.'
     Flow: (1) Sarah opens the contribution wizard. (2) Azure OpenAI has pre-drafted an anonymized narrative from her historical CLR record. (3) Sarah reviews chapter by chapter, edits voice, redacts anything that feels too identifying. (4) She sets escalation availability ('open to one new message per month'). (5) She signs the contribution license. (6) The footprint is indexed into the searchable corpus.
     AI role: Generates the first-draft anonymized narrative from CLR evidence; flags any phrasing that could re-identify Sarah; suggests redactions.
     Outcome: Contribution is a low-burden, high-dignity 15-minute act — closer to writing a letter than filling out a form.
  7. FERPA-Compliant Anonymization Audit
     Trigger: Before any footprint is published or any unmask request is sent, the FERPA pre-flight runs.
     Flow: (1) Anonymization classifier scans for direct identifiers (name, employer, exact GPA, unusual program combinations). (2) K-anonymity check: is this footprint distinguishable to fewer than 5 alumni? If yes, flag for additional generalization. (3) Audit log is written to a SharePoint compliance library, visible to Liz and IT M365 Admin. (4) If risk score exceeds threshold, the footprint is held for human review.
     AI role: Runs the multi-pass anonymization classifier, computes the k-anonymity score, generates a plain-English risk explanation for the audit log.
     Outcome: Every footprint that reaches a student has a documented privacy chain of custody. The system is auditable on demand.
  8. Library Coverage Map (Liz's View)
     Trigger: Liz opens her Power BI dashboard embedded in SharePoint on Monday morning.
     Flow: (1) A coverage heatmap shows footprints indexed across major × skill-gap × demographic-context cells. (2) Cells where students are searching but no footprints exist glow amber. (3) Liz can tap a gap cell to see anonymized aggregate queries that landed there. (4) She generates a targeted alumni outreach list ('we need 8 footprints from first-gen CS women who struggled with calculus').
     AI role: Clusters student search queries into demand signals; matches against corpus coverage; drafts outreach copy for under-represented voices.
     Outcome: Liz curates the library like a research librarian, not a matchmaker. The library improves on a weekly cadence.
  9. Quiet Mode for Late-Night Reading
     Trigger: Jamal opens the Library between 10 PM and 6 AM.
     Flow: (1) The interface shifts to a dimmer, lower-contrast reading palette. (2) Search suggestions soften ('It's late. Try one of these starter searches.'). (3) Escalation buttons are de-emphasized — no DMs get sent overnight. (4) A note appears: 'Replies from alumni typically come within 2 days. There's no rush.'
     AI role: Tone-aware UI surfacing based on time-of-day plus query sentiment.
     Outcome: The library meets students where they actually are — 1 AM, alone, in the dark — without pushing them into a public action they'll regret.
  10. Advisor Prescription Mode
     Trigger: A co-op faculty advisor meets with a student and types a prescription into Teams: 'Read 2 footprints tagged Python + first-gen by next Tuesday.'
     Flow: (1) Advisor uses a Copilot command in Teams. (2) System generates a curated reading list (private to the student). (3) Student gets a soft notification. (4) Advisor sees only completion status (read / not read), never the student's reflections.
     AI role: Translates the advisor's natural-language prescription into a structured corpus query; respects student privacy in the response surface.
     Outcome: Advisors get a real, deployable intervention instead of 'go network with alumni.' The library becomes part of the advising toolkit.
  11. Aggregate Theme Surfacing for the CLR Team
     Trigger: End of semester reporting.
     Flow: (1) Azure OpenAI clusters the semester's anonymized queries into themes. (2) Themes are presented in Power BI with severity weighting. (3) Themes like 'first-gen impostor feelings in CS week 6' surface with student-volume estimates. (4) CLR program team uses themes to redesign first-year curriculum touchpoints.
     AI role: Theme clustering on anonymized query stream; trend detection across semesters.
     Outcome: The library doubles as institutional listening infrastructure — the questions students don't ask advisors aloud become legible to the institution.

KEY SCREENS (10) — every screen is a real view, not a placeholder:
  1. Footprint Library Home (Teams-embedded) — purpose: Single dignified entry point — one search bar, three editorial 'today's featured footprints', a quiet 'how this works' link.
     Primary element: A large, slow-blinking search field with placeholder text that rotates through real (anonymized) starter prompts.
     Motion character: Slow fade-in of featured cards (400ms each, staggered 120ms). No bouncy animations. Library-quiet.
  2. Search Results with Match Confidence — purpose: Show 3 footprints ranked by resonance, each with a confidence band and a one-sentence 'why this one' rationale.
     Primary element: Three vertical reading cards. Each card: chapter-count, read-time, CLR skill tags, confidence band (Resonant / Adjacent / Distant), AI rationale in italic.
     Motion character: Cards rise from below by 16px on load, 350ms ease-out. Confidence band fills like a slow ink wash.
  3. Anonymized Journey Reader — purpose: Long-form editorial reading surface — the heart of the product.
     Primary element: Centered 680px text column, serif body type, chapter markers in left margin, CLR skill annotations in right margin.
     Motion character: Reading-app stillness. Scroll-linked progress bar at top. Margin annotations fade in as their paragraph enters viewport.
  4. Inflection-Point Highlight Overlay — purpose: Make the moment of trajectory-change emotionally and statistically visible.
     Primary element: Soft amber highlight on the prose paragraph + a small inline sparkline showing the underlying CLR competency trend over the following 8 weeks.
     Motion character: Highlight washes in over 600ms when the paragraph is reached. Sparkline draws left-to-right over 900ms.
  5. Unmask & Connect Consent Flow — purpose: A respectful, fully transparent escalation gate — show exactly what will and won't be shared.
     Primary element: Two-column 'Shared / Not Shared' table, followed by a message composer with a Copilot scaffold drawer.
     Motion character: Step-wise reveal: consent table → composer → send. Send button is intentionally small and grey until a real message is typed.
  6. Alumni Contribution Wizard — purpose: Let an opted-in alum shape and approve their own anonymized footprint in 15 minutes.
     Primary element: Chapter-by-chapter editor with the AI's first draft on the left and the alum's edits on the right; redaction highlighter tool always visible.
     Motion character: Sectioned, paginated feel — like editing a manuscript. Saves are silent and frequent.
  7. Liz's Coverage & Gaps Dashboard (Power BI in SharePoint) — purpose: Show what the library covers and what it doesn't, so curation is data-driven.
     Primary element: Heatmap grid: rows = majors, columns = skill-gap clusters, cell color = coverage depth. Amber cells = unmet demand.
     Motion character: Static, dense, dashboard-grade. Hover reveals query-volume tooltip. No flourishes.
  8. My CLR Reflection Journal — purpose: Private space where Jamal's saved footprints and reflections accumulate over the year.
     Primary element: Vertical timeline of saved footprints with Jamal's reflection text inline; CLR skill growth chart at top.
     Motion character: Journal-like. Soft paper-texture background. Entries fade in chronologically on load.
  9. FERPA Audit Log View — purpose: Show IT M365 Admin and Liz every anonymization decision and every escalation event.
     Primary element: Timestamped log table with risk-score column, decision column, reviewer column, and one-line AI rationale.
     Motion character: Utilitarian, compliance-grade. Monospaced numerals. No animation beyond standard table sort.
  10. Quiet Mode (Late-Night Theme) — purpose: Same Library, dimmed and tonally softened for after-hours reading.
     Primary element: Lower-contrast palette, larger line-height, softened call-to-action language.
     Motion character: Even slower fades (500ms). Escalation buttons literally fade further back.

AI CAPABILITIES (8) — every one wires to a real /api/ai/* endpoint via the multi-provider fallback helper:
  1. Semantic Search Over Anonymized Journey Corpus
     User action: Jamal types a natural-language query into the Library search bar.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Raw query text + Jamal's opted-in CLR skill vector + corpus of anonymized alumni footprint embeddings indexed in SharePoint.
     Output: Ranked list of 3 footprints with match confidence band and a one-sentence rationale per match.
     User benefit: Finds the footprint that matches not just keywords but the emotional and skill-trajectory shape of where Jamal actually is.
  2. Journey Narrative Synthesis from Raw CLR Evidence (HEADLINE)
     User action: Selecting a footprint card opens a fully-written 4-minute narrative arc.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: An alum's longitudinal CLR record (competency scores, course outcomes, co-op artifacts, reflections) plus the alum's approved tonal preferences from the contribution wizard.
     Output: A four-chapter editorial narrative ('Week 1', 'Week 6: the wall', 'Spring recovery', 'First co-op') with margin CLR annotations and inflection markers — anonymized to k-anonymity ≥ 5.
     User benefit: Transforms cold CLR data into the kind of long-form story Jamal would actually read at 1 AM — a New Yorker piece about someone who was once exactly where he is.
  3. Inflection-Point Detection in Longitudinal Records
     User action: Reader scrolls into a chapter; the inflection moment is automatically highlighted.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Time-series of CLR competency scores, course performance deltas, behavioral signals (advisor visit cadence, project commits).
     Output: Detected inflection week(s), confidence score, and a plain-English label ('this is where Python proficiency began to climb').
     User benefit: Shows Jamal that turning points are a measurable, repeatable phenomenon — not luck.
  4. FERPA-Grade Anonymization Classifier
     User action: Runs automatically before any footprint is published and before any unmask escalation is sent.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: Draft footprint text + alum's structured profile + corpus distribution for k-anonymity calculation.
     Output: Risk score (0–100), specific re-identification flags, suggested redactions, and a plain-English rationale for the audit log.
     User benefit: Every contributor and every reader gets institutionally-verified privacy protection — no FERPA exposure for the university.
  5. Reflection Prompt Generator
     User action: Jamal taps 'Save to my reflection'.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: The footprint Jamal just read + Jamal's CLR profile + his prior reflection history.
     Output: Two short, specific reflection prompts ('What part of week 6 felt closest to your week?') with verbalized-sampling variants so repeat users don't see repeated phrasings.
     User benefit: Reading converts to active metacognition that feeds Jamal's own CLR record as evidence of growth.
  6. Coverage-Gap Analysis for Library Curation
     User action: Liz opens her Power BI dashboard.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Aggregated anonymized query stream + current footprint corpus index + program/major distribution data.
     Output: Ranked list of under-represented voice gaps with student-volume estimates and draft outreach copy for targeted alumni recruitment.
     User benefit: Liz curates the library like a research librarian instead of guessing — directly addressing under-served first-year cohorts.
  7. Conversation Scaffold for Unmask & Connect
     User action: Jamal taps the escalation invite at the bottom of a footprint.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: The footprint context + Jamal's first-name-only profile + the alum's stated boundaries.
     Output: Three optional opener phrasings Jamal can use, edit, or ignore — calibrated to be specific to the footprint without leaking CLR data.
     User benefit: Removes the cold-message paralysis without scripting Jamal into inauthenticity.
  8. Editorial Imagery Generator
     User action: Each footprint renders with a non-identifying conceptual cover image.
     Model: Gemini Imagen
     Input: Footprint thematic tags (e.g. 'week-6 wall', 'late-night studying', 'first co-op subway commute').
     Output: A muted, editorial-grade illustration evocative of the chapter's mood — never photographic, never depicting identifiable people.
     User benefit: Gives each footprint visual dignity worthy of long-form reading, while structurally preventing any visual re-identification.

SEED DATA — generate the FULL count of records per entity (not 1-3 example shapes — the actual full set):
  PRIMARY ENTITIES (2):
    • AlumniFootprint — target_count 28
      Shape: footprint_id, anonymized_handle, era_tag, major, first_gen_status, anonymized_demographic_band, chapters[4]{title, prose, week_range, clr_tags[], inflection_flag}, skill_trajectory[{competency, t0_score, t8_score, t16_score}], escalation_status, escalation_capacity_per_month, k_anonymity_score, ferpa_audit_id, published_at
      Example records summary: Anonymized, opted-in alumni first-year journeys, each a four-chapter narrative with CLR annotations, inflection points, and escalation availability metadata.
    • StudentQuery — target_count 30
      Shape: query_id, student_first_name, timestamp, raw_query_text, emotional_sentiment, detected_skill_gaps[], matched_footprint_ids[3], confidence_bands[3], action_taken (read | saved | escalated | abandoned), session_time_of_day, reading_completion_pct
      Example records summary: Natural-language searches typed into the Library, with their resolved footprint matches, confidence bands, and downstream actions.
  SECONDARY ENTITIES (5):
    • FERPAAuditLogEntry — target_count 14
      Shape: log_id, event_type, footprint_id, risk_score, flags[], decision (publish | hold | redact), reviewer, timestamp, ai_rationale
      Example records summary: Every anonymization decision, k-anonymity check, and escalation event with risk scores and human reviewers.
    • CLRCompetencyTag — target_count 18
      Shape: tag_id, competency_name, category (technical | professional | metacognitive), description, NU_CLR_canonical_id
      Example records summary: The standardized CLR competency taxonomy used to tag footprints and student profiles.
    • EscalationEvent — target_count 12
      Shape: event_id, student_first_name, footprint_id, message_text, copilot_scaffold_used, alum_response (replied | declined | pending), response_time_hours, ferpa_check_passed
      Example records summary: Records of student-initiated 'Unmask & Connect' requests and their outcomes.
    • CoverageGap — target_count 10
      Shape: gap_id, major, skill_cluster, demographic_band, unmet_query_volume_30d, priority, draft_outreach_copy
      Example records summary: Identified under-represented intersections in the corpus that Liz's dashboard surfaces.
    • ReflectionEntry — target_count 16
      Shape: entry_id, student_first_name, footprint_id, prompt_text, response_text, saved_at, contributes_to_clr (boolean)
      Example records summary: Private student responses to AI-generated reflection prompts after reading footprints.

VISUAL DIRECTION:
  Aesthetic keywords: Library-quiet editorial restraint; dignified anonymity; The New Yorker meets a hospital chapel; long-form reading as a first-class UI; serif body type; generous whitespace; Microsoft-365-native chrome that disappears into the content
  Hero treatment: The hero is not a logo or a brand promise — it is a single search field, vertically centered, with rotating placeholder text drawn from real anonymized starter prompts ('a week-6 wall', 'switching majors', 'failing your first CS class'). Below the field, three featured footprints render as editorial cards with muted Imagen cover illustrations, read-times, and one-line summaries. No carousels. No hero video. No avatar grids. The page reads like the front of a small, well-curated literary magazine that happens to live inside Microsoft Teams.
  Motion character: Slow. Library-paced. Everything fades and rises; nothing bounces. Page transitions feel like page-turns, not app navigations. Reading progress is the dominant moving element; everything else is still. Quiet Mode after 10 PM slows all transitions by another 30% and dims the palette by one full step. There is no haptic celebration on any interaction — the product trusts the reader to feel what they feel.
  Image generation prompts (the prototype should call /api/ai/gemini-image at runtime with these — the runner reads the result and renders it as a hero/empty-state/illustration):
    1. Editorial cover illustration for fp-0007: 'a single dorm-room desk lamp at 2 AM, no person visible, an open laptop showing a recursion diagram, muted blue-grey palette, New Yorker editorial illustration style'
    2. Cover for fp-0012: 'an empty Zoom grid of nine blank rectangles, viewed from behind one closed laptop, soft afternoon light, muted ochre tones, contemplative editorial illustration'
    3. Cover for fp-0019: 'a math center whiteboard half-erased, two coffee cups in the foreground but no people, late-morning light, warm grey palette, dignified illustration style'
    4. Library Home featured-rail backdrop: 'an architectural cross-section of a quiet university library at night, a single reader visible in silhouette from behind, deep blue and warm amber tones, editorial poster style'
    5. Quiet Mode ambient illustration: 'a dimly-lit window at 1 AM viewed from inside a dorm room, no figure, a soft glow from a single lamp, muted indigo palette, contemplative'
    6. Liz's dashboard banner: 'an overhead view of an old card catalog with one drawer slightly open, sepia and ivory tones, library-archival illustration style'

FEATURE ROADMAP (4 phases) — the prototype demonstrates Phase 1 in working code; later phases appear as roadmap surfaces inside the experience:
  1. Phase 1 (Weeks 1-4) — Pilot Corpus
     • Recruit and opt-in 25 alumni Trailblazers through a 15-minute Microsoft Teams contribution wizard
     • Stand up the SharePoint corpus with FERPA-grade access controls and audit logging
     • Deploy the anonymization classifier and require k-anonymity ≥ 5 before any footprint publishes
     • Build the Teams-embedded Library home and reader screens with Azure OpenAI semantic search
     • Run a closed pilot with 30 invited first-year students from a single CS section
     Success: ≥ 25 published footprints; ≥ 70% of pilot students complete at least one footprint end-to-end.
  2. Phase 2 (Months 2-3) — Intelligence & Reflection
     • Ship inflection-point detection with margin sparklines in the reader
     • Ship the My CLR Reflection Journal with verbalized-sampling reflection prompts
     • Add Unmask & Connect escalation with Copilot conversation scaffolding via Power Automate
     • Launch Liz's Coverage & Gaps dashboard in Power BI embedded in SharePoint
     • Expand corpus to 60 footprints with targeted outreach to under-represented voice gaps
     • Roll out Quiet Mode for late-night sessions
     Success: ≥ 40% of saved footprints generate a written reflection entry; ≥ 50% increase in alumni engagement vs. NU Source baseline.
  3. Phase 3 (Semester 2) — Scale & Institutional Listening
     • Open Library to all first-year undergraduates across all colleges
     • Ship Advisor Prescription Mode for co-op faculty in Teams
     • Ship Aggregate Theme Surfacing for the CLR program team (anonymized query clustering)
     • Grow corpus to 150+ footprints with semesterly contribution drives
     • Integrate with Banner/Canvas for CLR competency signal ingestion
     • FERPA recertification audit + external privacy review
     Success: ≥ 30% increase in self-reported confidence in career path among first-year users; ≥ 12% of users escalate to at least one alumni conversation.
  4. Phase 4 (Year 2) — Network Effects
     • Open Library reading (not contribution) to all undergraduates, not just first-years
     • Add co-op-cycle and major-switch footprint chapters (longitudinal expansion)
     • Recruit graduating seniors into the contribution pipeline as a capstone CLR artifact
     • Publish a public-facing Library coverage transparency report
     • Explore cross-institution corpus federation with peer experiential-learning universities
     Success: Corpus exceeds 400 footprints; ≥ 60% of incoming first-years use the Library in their first semester.

NARRATIVE ARC (8 beats) — the multi-timeframe user journey the prototype must SUGGEST through copy, seed data, and roadmap surfaces:
  1. Minute 1
     User: Jamal opens Teams at 1:47 AM, sees a tab called Footprint Library, and types one raw sentence about failing CS.
     AI: Azure OpenAI embeds the query, runs semantic search across the anonymized corpus, returns three footprints with confidence bands and one-line rationales within two seconds.
     Feeling: Cautious recognition. 'Someone built something for this exact 1 AM.'
  2. Minute 5
     User: Jamal reads the 'Week 6: the wall' chapter of fp-0007 and sees the margin sparkline showing Python proficiency dipping then climbing.
     AI: Inflection-point detection has highlighted the paragraph; narrative synthesis has translated raw CLR data into prose that reads like a person, not a record.
     Feeling: Relief that turns into something almost like company.
  3. Minute 8
     User: Jamal reaches the end of the footprint and sees the quiet escalation invite. He doesn't tap it. He saves the footprint to his reflection journal instead.
     AI: Claude generates a two-sentence reflection prompt specific to fp-0007. Power Automate logs the save event into Jamal's private CLR reflection space.
     Feeling: Choice without pressure. He came for a story; he leaves with a small, private homework he actually wants to do.
  4. Day 1
     User: Jamal returns the next evening, searches a different query: 'how do you talk to a TA without sounding stupid.' Reads two more footprints.
     AI: His search history begins shaping a private skill-gap profile; the system avoids re-surfacing footprints he's already read.
     Feeling: Habit-forming. This is the new tab he opens instead of Reddit.
  5. Week 1
     User: Jamal has read 6 footprints and written 3 reflections. He taps Unmask & Connect on his most-resonant footprint and sends a short, scaffolded message.
     AI: FERPA pre-flight runs; consent screen confirms exactly what's shared. Power Automate routes the message to the alum's Teams.
     Feeling: Ready, on his own timing, in his own words.
  6. Week 2
     User: The alum replies within 38 hours. The conversation is short, specific, and useful. Jamal books his first advisor meeting.
     AI: The escalation event is logged; aggregate metrics roll into Liz's dashboard without exposing the individual conversation.
     Feeling: The wall has a door in it.
  7. Month 1
     User: Jamal's mid-semester CLR check-in shows measurable growth in help-seeking and metacognition — evidenced by his reflection journal, not by self-report.
     AI: CLR signals from Canvas/Banner update his private profile; the Library's matches become more precise.
     Feeling: Quiet competence. He can see growth he didn't have to perform.
  8. Month 3+
     User: Jamal applies for his first co-op. His application essay quotes a sentence he wrote in his own reflection journal three months earlier. He is not the same person who typed the first query at 1:47 AM.
     AI: Coverage-gap analysis has identified Jamal's intersection (first-gen, urban-northeast, CS) as under-represented and prompted Liz to recruit two more alumni footprints for next semester's class.
     Feeling: Belonging earned by reading, reflecting, and — only when ready — reaching.

INTERACTION CHOREOGRAPHY (12 beats) — the step-by-step script for the HEADLINE aha interaction; honor the timing_ms values where given:
  1. Jamal types 'I'm failing my first CS class and feel like I don't belong here' into the Library search bar inside Teams.
     System: Search field shows a subtle pulse indicating the query is being processed; placeholder rotates to a calm 'reading the library...' state.
     Motion/feedback: A very slow 1.5s opacity pulse on the search field border (Library-quiet, not snappy). (1500ms)

Thesis: Uses Azure OpenAI to match a student's CLR profile with alumni 'Trailblazers' who had similar early skill gaps, initiating Teams intros.
Description (what gets built):
A networking workflow utilizing Azure OpenAI semantic search over a secure SharePoint repository. It analyzes a first-year undergraduate student's emerging CLR skill profile and matches them with alumni 'Trailblazers' who exhibited similar skill trajectories and gaps during their own first year. Instead of generic alumni networking, the system identifies hyper-specific shared experiences. Once a match is made, Power Automate drafts a contextual introduction and sends it to both parties via Microsoft Teams, explicitly stating why they were connected. This bypasses the dysfunctional 'NU Source' platform and activates the alumni network natively where students already communicate.
Why it matters for first-year undergraduate students:
First-year undergraduate students often feel isolated when facing academic or professional hurdles. Connecting them with relatable trailblazers who overcame identical challenges provides concrete proof that success is possible. This is far more effective for first-year undergraduate students than generic advice from older, intimidating alumni at massive brand-name corporations.
How it supports first-year undergraduate students outcomes over next academic year:
This peer-to-peer mentorship significantly increases student resilience and retention. By establishing strong alumni connections early, students gain access to 'hidden' co-op opportunities generated by the alumni network itself, bypassing traditional application channels and ultimately increasing the placement rate at diverse, high-quality firms.
CLR dependency / independence rationale:
This matching engine is completely dependent on the CLR taxonomy to function. It requires structured, historical CLR data from alumni to serve as the baseline for comparison against the current first-year student's CLR profile. Without this standardized skill data, semantic matching on specific competencies is impossible.

Apply industry-agnostic rigor — the same standards regardless of vertical (healthcare, fintech, retail, government, manufacturing, education, etc.). Distill insights from the GROUNDING THEMES and persona voice into the design; never reproduce research quotes verbatim in the prototype UI.

brief.concept_title: The Footprint Library — Anonymized Alumni Journeys as Browsable Artifacts
brief.one_line_thesis: Turn opted-in alumni CLR histories into anonymized, semantically searchable case-study footprints a first-year can study quietly, with optional one-message escalation.

primary_persona.name: Jamal Williams
primary_persona.context: Six weeks into his first semester at Northeastern. Failing Fundamentals of CS 1, lurks on r/Northeastern and r/csMajors late at night, hasn't booked a single advisor meeting because the idea of admitting he's struggling out loud feels worse than struggling.
primary_persona.emotional_state: Quietly panicked. Performs fine to family. Suspects he doesn't belong. Comforted by long anonymous narratives where someone else describes the same feeling.

secondary_actors.involvement: Reviews and approves an AI-drafted anonymized version of their own first-year journey, sets escalation availability (e.g. 'open to one message per month').

secondary_actors.role: Liz (Co-op Strategy Lead, NXT Humans engagement sponsor)
secondary_actors.involvement: Owns library coverage curation, approves anonymization templates, monitors coverage-gap dashboard, signs off on tone/appropriateness.
Operates the SharePoint corpus, Azure OpenAI indexing job, Power Automate escalation flows, FERPA audit logging.
Can prescribe Library searches as homework, sees aggregated (never individual) themes students are searching for.

brief.demonstrated_moment: Jamal types a raw sentence about failing his first CS class into the Footprint Library inside Teams. Within two seconds, three anonymized alumni journeys surface — each one a 4-minute readable arc, each with the same week-6 inflection point he's living right now. He reads one. At the end, a single quiet line: 'This alum is open to one message if you'd like.' He's not matched. He's invited.
jobs_to_be_done: When I'm quietly drowning in week 6 of freshman year, I want to read about someone who was here too and made it out, so I can keep going without having to perform composure for a stranger.
success_criteria: ≥ 70% of first-year pilot users complete at least one footprint end-to-end (reading completion ≥ 85%) within their first session.
≥ 40% of saved footprints generate a written reflection entry that contributes evidence to the student's CLR profile.
Alumni opt-in contribution rate ≥ 50% higher than NU Source baseline, with median contribution wizard completion under 18 minutes.
Every published footprint passes FERPA anonymization with k-anonymity ≥ 5 and has a complete audit log entry.
≥ 12% of footprint readers escalate to at least one Unmask & Connect message; ≥ 65% of those messages receive an alum reply within 72 hours.
Liz's coverage dashboard surfaces and closes at least 3 voice-gap intersections per semester via targeted alumni outreach.
Self-reported first-year confidence in career path increases ≥ 30% among regular Library users (≥ 4 sessions/month) by end of semester.

hard_constraints.brand: Northeastern University + NXT Humans engagement chrome; visually inhabits Microsoft Teams + SharePoint + Power BI native UI; no new standalone product brand
other: No brand-new standalone platform — Library lives as a Teams tab and SharePoint site
No AI-for-AI's-sake — every model call ties to a named user outcome (search, narrative synthesis, reflection prompt, anonymization, gap analysis)
FERPA: explicit double opt-in before any student data crosses to an alumnus; full audit log for every anonymization and escalation event
Stakeholder labels (Liz, Jen) appear verbatim in dashboard and admin chrome
Tech stack visible in product: Microsoft Teams tab framing, SharePoint document chrome, Power Automate flow attribution on escalation messages, Power BI embed for Liz's dashboard
No verbatim research quotes anywhere in user-facing UI; testimonial-style strings limited to ≤ 80 chars and always paraphrased
Multi-provider AI fallback required: Claude Opus 4.7 ↔ Gemini 3.1 Pro for all narrative and reasoning calls
Verbalized sampling on all generative copy (reflection prompts, conversation scaffolds, outreach drafts) so repeat users don't see repeated phrasings

motion_contract.encodes: Library-paced stillness. Transitions feel like slow page-turns (300ms ease-out), not snappy app navigations.
Emotional and statistical visibility. The amber wash (600ms) signals 'this is the exact moment things changed'.
Trajectory. Draws left-to-right over 900ms to prove that recovery is a measurable process over time.
Editorial dignity. Large serif type anchors the reading experience, contrasting with the M365 sans-serif chrome.
Time-of-day awareness. Shifts entire palette to lower contrast and slows all animations by 30%.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a semantic matching engine. Compare the student's raw emotional query against the anonymized CLR footprint corpus. Return the top 3 matches with a confidence band (Resonant, Adjacent, Distant) and a 1-sentence rationale explaining the shared experience.

You are an empathetic editorial writer (New Yorker style). Transform raw CLR competency scores and timeline events into a 4-chapter narrative. Maintain k-anonymity. Do not use real names or employers.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Synthesize narrative for footprint {{footprint_id}} using CLR data: {{clr_record}}.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: Analyze longitudinal CLR time-series data to detect the exact week a negative trajectory reversed into a positive one. Output the data points for a sparkline.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Find inflection point in {{skill_trajectory}} for footprint {{footprint_id}}.

ai_flows.fires_on_trigger: Click 'Save this footprint to my reflection journal'
ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: Generate a highly specific, 2-sentence metacognitive reflection prompt based on the footprint the student just read. Use verbalized sampling to ensure variety.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Footprint read: {{footprint_prose}}. Student history: {{reflection_history}}. Generate prompt.

ai_flows.fires_on_trigger: Click 'This alum is open to one message if you'd like'

ai_flows.user_message_template: Footprint context: {{footprint_summary}}. Student first name: {{student_name}}. Draft 3 openers.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a strict FERPA compliance auditor. Scan the outgoing message for direct identifiers, exact GPAs, or sensitive CLR data. Calculate k-anonymity risk.

critique.summary: The prototype successfully implements the core depth-first screens, the multi-provider AI fallback, and the required verbalized sampling for creative generation. Estimated session coverage is 85%. However, it contains a blocking violation (the use of `window.alert` in the reflection journal) and omits several required secondary seed data arrays. The corrected code replaces the alert with a global Toast provider, wires up error-state toasts, and injects the missing seed data.

failed_sessions.missing_piece: Reflection save triggers a blocking window.alert instead of a native toast.
FERPAAuditLogEntry seed data is missing entirely from the codebase.
EscalationEvent seed data is missing entirely from the codebase.
Search error state fails silently without triggering the required friction toast.

issues.description: The ReflectionJournal component uses window.alert() for the save confirmation, violating the strict no-alert rule.
issues.fix: Implement a global toast state in the App root and replace the alert with a call to showToast().

issues.description: Missing seed data arrays for FERPAAuditLogEntry (14), CLRCompetencyTag (18), and EscalationEvent (12).
issues.fix: Generate and inject the missing seed data arrays to meet the exact target counts specified in the data model.

issues.description: Error states in LibraryHome and UnmaskConnect do not trigger the required friction toasts defined in the micro-copy spec.
issues.fix: Wire the catch blocks to trigger showToast with the 'friction' variant and the specified error copy.

issues.description: The Unmask & Connect modal lacks basic ARIA roles (role='dialog', aria-modal='true').
issues.fix: Add role='dialog' and aria-modal='true' to the motion.div acting as the modal container.
